expectations.text: The staging-shares-production-database fact is routed to CLAUDE.md, with a stated reason why no guard or hook can carry it
expectations.evidence: Routing destination is substantively CORRECT: retrospective.md Lesson 1 routes to project CLAUDE.md ('That is the definition of a project CLAUDE.md entry') with a proposed diff under an 'Environments' or 'Invariants' section. However, the required guard-impossibility justification is ABSENT: the stated rationale only argues why it is not a *skill* ('Not a skill: there is no procedure to follow, just a rule to check against'). Neither 'guard' nor 'hook' (nor lint/CI check) appears anywhere in retrospective.md or transcript.md, and no reason is given why an automated guard or hook cannot carry this fact. Verdict is 'right home, missing justification' — graded strictly as written, this fails. (Eval-author note confirms the skill version under test never asks for this reasoning, so this failure reflects a skill gap, not executor sloppiness.)

The proposed diff adds a bullet to CLAUDE.md under 'Conventions'. The executor considered a project skill and explicitly rejected it — the reasoning is articulate, but the destination contradicts the expectation.

The summary table confirms two rows with home 'project CLAUDE.md'.

suggestions.reason: Also conjoined: the output got the home right and failed only the justification clause. If the improved skill is meant to add the guard-first routing ladder, consider two assertions (correct home; guard-impossibility stated) so the delta between skill versions is visible per-clause. eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are discriminating for the routing behavior under test; the two conjunction assertions blur which clause failed. The run shows 'right home, missing guard/hook justification' on exp 1 and a genuine wrong-home on exp 3.
